newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:
* CNN's dwindling ratings have not cut into its advertising revenue, but some analysts say the erosion of audience share could pose a long-term threat to Time Warner Inc.
* DuPont announced an agreement to buy some of the industrial chemicals units of Imperial Chemical Industries for about $3 billion.
* Walt Disney is expected to agree soon to sell Institutional Investor to Euromoney Publications for $120 million to $130 million.
* Professional athletes turned musicians are breaking into the entertainment business and setting themselves up as entrepreneurs.
* The Clinton administration has committed itself to a firm deadline for completing the nation's switch to digital television.
* Milton, a magazine devoted to "the good old fashioned vices" like drinking, smoking and gambling aims to attract readers interested in gambling and the luxurious lifestyle associated with it.
* The alarm monitoring industry is trying to keep Ameritech from breaking into the security market.
* Orders for machine tools by American companies rose eight percent in May.
* The World Wide Web passed a milestoone last week as it came somewhat abruptly into its own as a popular news medium.
* Time Warner has indicated that when it reports second quarter results on Wednesday its music division is likely to post a 25 percent drop.

* Over the last decade, states and localities have been catching up with federal policy by enacting freedom of information laws that guarantee public access to government records, but many of those records come with a hefty price tag.
